stories.title: Here are the 30,000 songs Sony is suing Udio’s AI music generator over
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Sony Music is suing the AI music generator Udio over copyright infringement.
The lawsuit claims Udio infringed on over 30,000 songs, including tracks by major artists like Elvis Presley and Beyoncé.
This case highlights major ongoing legal battles regarding AI training data and intellectual property rights in the music industry.

The presence of 'safetensors' indicates modern, secure model handling practices.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.

The tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.author: unknown

The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million from prominent investors like Y Combinator and Benchmark.
The company boasts a large developer base, currently serving 8.9 million developers.
The news highlights the growing commercial and adoption success of open-source large language model serving platforms.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance gain is achieved through the use of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to 90% speed improvement, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model outputs.
The updates also result in faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these personal AI agents entirely on local, private hardware.
It integrates native support for Ollama, leveraging local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, has integrated MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets and optimizes execution on Apple Silicon hardware.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, indicating ongoing development.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with existing messaging applications.
Its core functionality involves connecting these apps to local AI coding agents.
A key feature is that all AI processing runs entirely on the user's local device, emphasizing privacy.

stories.title: Ford’s $30,000 electric truck: all the news about the company’s big EV re-do
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Ford is pivoting its electric vehicle strategy after the initial F-150 Lightning did not meet market expectations.
The automaker is developing a new Universal Electric Vehicle Platform for future models.
The first vehicle under this new platform is slated to be a $30,000 electric truck.

stories.title: Judge halts Paramount's $111B purchase of Warner Bros. in win for US states
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A judge has issued a restraining order against Paramount's proposed $111B acquisition of Warner Bros.
The legal action is based on the finding that the merger is likely to violate antitrust laws.
This ruling represents a significant regulatory hurdle for major media consolidation in the US.

stories.title: AliExpress hit with record $625M fine after failing to make EU-ordered fixes
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: AliExpress received a record $625M fine from EU regulators.
The fine stems from the retailer's failure to implement required fixes under the Digital Services Act (DSA).
The incident highlights increasing regulatory scrutiny and enforcement power within the EU's digital market.

stories.title: Pay up or not? Ransomware surge has victims facing tough choices.
stories.author: Hannah Murphy, Financial Times
bullet_points: Ransomware attacks are becoming significantly more sophisticated.
Governments are actively considering legislation to ban ransom payments.
The trend forces victims into difficult strategic decisions regarding payment.

stories.title: CRAFT: Clustering Rubrics to Diagnose Weak LLM Capabilities and Generate Targeted Fine-Tuning Data
stories.author: Yunzhong He
bullet_points: CRAFT introduces a method to move beyond simple performance measurement in LLM evaluations.
It converts rubric-based evaluation datasets into specific diagnoses of underlying weak LLM capabilities.
The tool facilitates the generation of targeted fine-tuning data to address identified failure modes.

stories.title: Harmonizing AI Safety Thresholds
stories.author: Markov Grey
bullet_points: Frontier AI companies lack standardized capability thresholds, hindering third-party verification and cross-company comparison.
The absence of common minimum safety thresholds risks inconsistent risk mitigation and a 'race to the bottom' in safety standards.
The paper proposes a methodology to derive harmonized safety thresholds across three distinct risk domains (including misuse risks).

stories.title: PagedWeight: Efficient MoE LLM Serving with Dynamic Quality-Aware Weight Quantization
stories.author: Sasa Misailovic
bullet_points: Introduces PagedWeight, a novel serving method for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs.
Addresses the memory tension between large MoE model weights and growing KV cache during inference.
Achieves efficiency by dynamically quantizing MoE model weights at runtime, balancing precision and cache size.

stories.title: Learning Standard Model structure from LHC data with Riemannian flow matching
stories.author: Oleg Ruchayskiy
bullet_points: Introduces ShellFlow, a Riemannian conditional flow matching model, to learn the Standard Model structure from LHC data.
The model uses a single transformer-based generative approach to cover a vast range of invariant masses (sub-GeV to TeV continuum).
It generates particles on their on-shell manifold, relying only on the on-shell condition as a physics prior.

stories.title: Frontier AI performance across the business disciplines: a case-grounded benchmark of knowledge work and analytical reasoning
stories.author: Mitch Weiss
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in current LLM evaluation by focusing on analytical knowledge work, rather than just factual recall or coding.
It proposes a case-grounded benchmark to measure LLM performance in complex tasks like synthesizing information and exercising judgment.
This research highlights that existing AI benchmarks fail to adequately capture the nuanced capabilities required by white-collar professionals.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also introduces web search capabilities to Claude Code.
This enhances the functionality of AI coding assistants by adding complex reasoning and real-time data access.

stories.title: The FCC is planning to retroactively ban disguised DJI gadgets
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: The FCC is preparing to use its authority to retroactively ban certain gadgets.
The crackdown specifically targets devices linked to 'DJI front companies'.
This action leverages FCC power granted previously to ban already-approved imports.

stories.title: SpaceX in your index fund, explained
stories.author: Elizabeth Lopatto
bullet_points: The article discusses the implications of a high-risk, high-reward company like SpaceX being included in a broad market index fund (Nasdaq-100).
It contrasts the safety perception of index funds with the volatility and speculative nature of individual, high-growth tech stocks.
The core theme is the tension between diversified, low-risk investing strategies and the inclusion of speculative 'giant gamble' companies.

stories.title: LG’s monitors come with an unwanted addition for Windows: McAfee pop-up ads
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: LG monitors are silently installing driver updates and the LG Monitor App Installer via Windows Update.
The installation process occurs without any user permission prompts or notifications on Windows 11.
The installed LG app lacks visible user controls, raising concerns about unwanted software.

stories.title: Firefighting drones in the works as wildfires plague US nearly year-round
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Wildfire mitigation is a growing focus, with technology being tested to address the issue.
The story highlights the use of firefighting drones in ongoing efforts against US wildfires.
A specific XPRIZE competition is testing the efficacy of these drones for early wildfire intervention in California.

stories.title: The Space Force is now seeking to buy up to $30 billion in rocket launches
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: The U.S. Space Force is being tasked with a significant increase in launch operations.
The scope of this requirement involves procuring up to $30 billion worth of rocket launches.
The increased demand is linked to directives from the Trump administration.

stories.title: RIP bargain bin: The price impact of Sony's disc-free PlayStation plan
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Sony's new disc-free PlayStation plan is impacting consumer purchasing habits.
The plan challenges the traditional value proposition of physical game discs.
The article suggests used physical discs may remain a more cost-effective option than digital discounts.

stories.title: Evaluating Open-Weight LLMs for Generating Structured Threat Information for Autonomous Vehicle Vulnerabilities
stories.author: Md Rayhanur Rahman
bullet_points: The research focuses on using Open-Weight Large Language Models (LLMs) to process cybersecurity data.
The goal is to convert unstructured vulnerability data (like CVE entries) into structured information relevant for Autonomous Vehicle (AV) security.
This addresses the critical need for structured threat intelligence to secure complex CAV components (sensors, ECUs, etc.).

stories.title: When Does Muon Help Agentic Reinforcement Learning?
stories.author: Hao Sun
bullet_points: The paper investigates the utility of the Muon optimizer in agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training, comparing it to AdamW.
Applying Muon specifically to hidden weight matrices within the Group-in-Group Policy Optimization (GiGPO) framework significantly boosted validation success from 0.290 to 0.546.
The results suggest Muon offers a substantial advantage in sparse-reward agentic RL tasks over standard high-rate AdamW controls.

stories.title: An Exam for Active Observers
stories.author: Willie Neiswanger
bullet_points: The paper addresses the concept of 'active observation' in human vision, where gaze is continuously redirected based on hypotheses.
It posits that current vision-language benchmarks fail to empirically test whether Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) exhibit active observation.
The authors introduce ActiveVision, a new benchmark designed to make active observation a measurable metric for ML models.

stories.title: When Do Multi-Agent Systems Help? An Information Bottleneck Perspective
stories.author: Shuiwang Ji
bullet_points: The paper investigates the performance advantages of Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) versus Single-Agent Systems (SAS) powered by LLMs.
It introduces an Information Bottleneck perspective to theoretically explain the differences in performance between MAS and SAS.
A key finding suggests SAS maintains a full reasoning trace in a shared context, whereas MAS utilizes isolated local contexts connected by bounds.

stories.title: ToolSciVer: Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification with Visual Tool Augmented Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Rui Zhang
bullet_points: ToolSciVer is a new framework designed for Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification (MSCV).
It addresses limitations in current methods by using visual tool augmentation to locate and interpret evidence from figures and tables in scientific papers.
The framework integrates multimodal observations into reliable reasoning to verify complex scientific claims.

stories.title: A Methodology for Auditable Trustworthiness Levels in AI Lifecycle Governance
stories.author: Andrea Ferrario
bullet_points: Proposes a lightweight methodology for establishing auditable trustworthiness levels in AI systems.
Addresses the gap where existing AI trustworthiness research is either too abstract for lifecycle monitoring or too narrow for governance needs.
Focuses on documenting changes in AI trustworthiness in a transparent and contestable manner for governance.

stories.title: Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training
stories.author: Pavel Izmailov
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap between LLM pretraining and subsequent Reinforcement Learning (RL) fine-tuning.
It seeks to answer how pretraining choices (like model size and data) influence the effectiveness of RL compute.
The research aims to elucidate the specific functional changes that RL induces within the LLM architecture.

stories.title: Physics-enhanced reinforcement learning for real-time optimal control of dynamical systems
stories.author: Andrea Manzoni
bullet_points: The paper addresses the sample inefficiency of Reinforcement Learning (RL) when applied to complex, nonlinear dynamical systems.
It proposes integrating physics knowledge to enhance RL, aiming to overcome the limitations imposed by the curse of dimensionality.
This research is relevant for improving real-time optimal control in systems where extensive environmental interaction is costly or impossible.

stories.title: When Does Muon Help Agentic Reinforcement Learning?
stories.author: Hao Sun
bullet_points: The paper investigates the utility of the optimizer 'Muon' specifically within agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training.
Applying Muon only to hidden weight matrices during GiGPO significantly improved final-window validation success (from 0.290 to 0.546) compared to high-rate AdamW controls.
While Muon is competitive with AdamW in large-scale pre-training, its specific benefit in sparse-reward agentic RL remains a key area of study.

stories.title: An Exam for Active Observers
stories.author: Willie Neiswanger
bullet_points: The paper addresses the concept of 'active observation' in human vision, where gaze is continuously guided by hypotheses rather than static snapshots.
It highlights a gap in current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and vision-language benchmarks regarding whether they exhibit this active observation.
The authors introduce 'ActiveVision,' a new benchmark designed to empirically measure active observation capabilities in ML models.

stories.title: PRISA: Proactive Infrastructure LiDAR Framework for Intersection Safety Assessment
stories.author: Hoang H. Nguyen
bullet_points: Introduces PRISA, a new LiDAR framework designed for proactive safety assessment at urban intersections.
Focuses on real-time, continuous monitoring to anticipate traffic conflicts involving vehicles and vulnerable road users (VRUs).
Leverages privacy-preserving and low-light-robust roadside sensors for long-term traffic observation.

stories.title: An Exam for Active Observers
stories.author: Willie Neiswanger
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap in current benchmarks regarding whether Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) perform 'active observation,' a concept central to human vision.
Active observation, where gaze is continuously redirected based on hypotheses, is presented as a critical cognitive function for effective perception.
The authors introduce 'ActiveVision,' a new benchmark designed specifically to empirically measure active observation capabilities in ML models.

stories.title: ToolSciVer: Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification with Visual Tool Augmented Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Rui Zhang
bullet_points: ToolSciVer is a novel framework designed for Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification (MSCV).
It addresses limitations in existing methods by integrating visual evidence (figures, tables, charts) with textual context.
The framework utilizes tool-augmented Reinforcement Learning to improve the location and interpretation of decisive visual evidence.

stories.title: Rate-Utility Frontiers for Language Encodings: Comparing Tokens, Bytes, and Pixels Under Controlled Linguistic Content
stories.author: Desmond Elliott
bullet_points: The research compares three different text encoding methods (tokens, bytes, and pixels) used in language models.
The study controls for linguistic content and downstream modeling capacity to provide a fairer comparison across languages.
It utilizes verified parallel sentences across thirteen languages and five scripts to evaluate encoding preservation.

stories.title: Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training
stories.author: Pavel Izmailov
bullet_points: The research addresses the gap between LLM pretraining and subsequent Reinforcement Learning (RL) fine-tuning.
It seeks to answer how pretraining choices (like model size and data) influence the effectiveness of RL compute.
The study aims to elucidate the specific mechanisms by which RL alters the model's behavior for complex reasoning.

stories.title: Frontier Language Models Struggle to Copy: Text Can Be Better Viewed in 2D
stories.author: Kaifeng Lyu
bullet_points: Frontier Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit unexpected failures in a basic task: perfectly copying an input string.
The research attributes this failure to the limitations of positional encodings within Transformer architectures.
The models' inductive bias favors local context matching shortcuts over precise positional retrieval.

stories.title: Loop the Loopies!
stories.author: Bryan Dai
bullet_points: Introduction of 'Loopie,' a new series of powerful looped Transformer models.
The models utilize a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, featuring 20B and 6B parameter variants.
Loopie addresses a known limitation in looped Transformers regarding scaling compute versus parameter count.

stories.title: Nativ: Run frontier open models locally on your Mac
stories.author: aratahikaru5
bullet_points: Nativ allows users to run frontier open-source AI models locally on macOS.
This addresses the growing desire for local, private AI inference.
It lowers the barrier to entry for running powerful LLMs without cloud dependency.

stories.title: AI And Code Ownership: Who Is Responsible For Generated Code?
stories.author: nazar-boyko
bullet_points: The article addresses the complex legal question of code ownership when AI generates software.
It highlights the uncertainty surrounding intellectual property rights for AI-assisted code.
This topic is relevant to developers and legal professionals navigating AI integration.

stories.title: AI Coding Agents Can Make Junior Developers Faster. Can They Still Make Them Better?
stories.author: balrajola
bullet_points: AI coding agents have the potential to increase the speed at which junior developers can deliver code.
There is a concern that reliance on AI tools might hinder the long-term skill development of junior developers.
The article poses a critical question about the balance between speed enhancement and quality/mastery development.
